text:
You need a fast, creative way to generate a wide range of cannabis-themed art concepts for acrylic board displays across a large dispensary, with room to explore rough directions first and refine what works.

I’m Noor Halden, and I’d love to help with the concepting phase and the follow-up refinement. I have 6 years of experience working with Python-based AI and NLP tools, including PyTorch, scikit-learn, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, pandas, and machine learning workflows. While my background is technical rather than traditional illustration, I’ve worked on AI systems where generating strong, usable outputs quickly and iterating based on feedback was the core requirement.

One relevant project was a Contract clause search assistant for a legal client. I built an assistant that answers questions over 9,000 contracts and always quotes the clause and page it used. Using Python, LangChain, OpenAI API, pgvector, PostgreSQL, and FastAPI, the system achieved 0.91 faithfulness on a 120-question lawyer-written test set, and reduced clause lookup time from 25 minutes to 3 minutes. That project required careful prompt design, structured iteration, and making outputs useful for real-world review, which maps well to your need for a first-pass batch of concept ideas followed by refinement.

For your dispensary, I’d approach this as a rapid concept-generation engagement: start with a 30-minute ideation session, produce a broad spread of rough directions, and organize them into clear thematic buckets so you can quickly see what fits the space. Since your themes include cannabis, terpenes, smoke, and open-ended creative ideas, I’d focus on variety, visual impact, and art that can translate well to large printed acrylic panels.

I can help you think through concept directions that feel cohesive across the dispensary while still giving each piece its own character. If you already have a sense of the mood you want, I can use that to steer the first round of concepts; if not, I can help explore options and narrow them down based on what resonates.

Would you like the first round of concepts to lean more surreal and artistic, or more clean and modern for the acrylic boards?
